why: A queue is a singly linked list with a head (dequeue end) and a tail (enqueue end). delete and removeAllDuplicates are the classic 'unlink a node using its predecessor' moves; the trap is keeping the tail pointer correct when the removed node is the last one.
hints: Hold three things: head, tail and a Node class with val and next. Enqueue links after tail; dequeue advances head.
To remove a node from a singly linked list you need its predecessor: walk with prev/cur (a dummy node before head makes removing the head the same case as any other).

removeAllDuplicates is one pass with a seen set: unlink cur when its value is already seen, else add it. After any removal, if you unlinked the last node, set tail = prev. O(n) per delete/dedupe, O(1) for enqueue/dequeue.
pitfalls: Deleting the tail node without moving tail makes the next enqueue attach to a detached node (example 2).
When dequeue empties the queue, set tail to None as well as head.
delete removes only the first match from the head, not every match.
